<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Introductory Note. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At 12:03 a.m., New York City time, on October&#160;1, 2026 (the &#8220;Effective Time&#8221;), Corteva, Inc. (&#8220;Corteva&#8221;) completed its previously announced separation into two independent, publicly traded companies through the separation (&#8220;Separation&#8221;) of Corteva&#8217;s seed operating segment into an independent, publicly traded company, Vylor Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;). The Separation was effected through a pro rata distribution of all of the outstanding shares of common stock, par value $0.01 per share, of the Company (&#8220;Company common stock&#8221;) to holders of common stock, par value $0.01 per share, of Corteva as of the close of business on September&#160;24, 2026 (the &#8220;Distribution&#8221;). Additional information about the Distribution can be found in the Company&#8217;s information statement, dated September&#160;24, 2026, which was included as Exhibit 99.1 to the Company&#8217;s Current Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">8-K</span> filed on September&#160;25, 2026 (the &#8220;Information Statement&#8221;), on August 6, 2026, under the section entitled &#8220;The Spin-Off&#8221;, which section is incorporated by reference herein. </p> <p style="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:11%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">Item&#8201;2.01</span></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:left">Completion of Acquisition or Disposition of Assets. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The information set forth in the Introductory Note of this Current Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">8-K</span> is incorporated by reference into this Item 2.01. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At 12:01 a.m., New York City time, on October 1, 2026, in connection with the Separation, the Company issued to EIDP, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Corteva (&#8220;EIDP&#8221;), 667,302,930 shares of Company common stock (the &#8220;New Company Shares&#8221;). The New Company Shares were subsequently distributed to Corteva and thereafter distributed in the Distribution. EIDP contributed to the Company 100% of the issued and outstanding shares of capital stock of Pioneer Hi-Bred International, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company (&#8220;PHI&#8221;), in exchange for (i) New Company Shares, (ii) payment of a cash distribution by the Company to EIDP in an aggregate amount equal to approximately $761 million (subject to certain adjustments) and (iii) the assumption by the Company of a portion of EIDP&#8217;s $500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 2.300% Senior Notes due July 2030, $500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.125% Senior Notes due May 2032 and $600,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 4.800% Senior Notes due May 2033 (such senior notes, collectively the &#8220;EIDP Notes&#8221;) in connection with the private offers to exchange any and all of the outstanding EIDP Notes, to the extent held by eligible holders, for new notes of the corresponding series issued by the Company. The New Company Shares were issued without registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the &#8220;Securities Act&#8221;), in reliance on the exemptions provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act as a transaction not involving a public offering and in reliance on similar exemptions under applicable state laws. </p> <p style="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:11%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">Item&#8201;2.03</span></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:left">Creation of a Direct Financial Obligation or an Obligation under an <span style="white-space:nowrap">Off-Balance</span> Sheet Arrangement of a Registrant. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The information set forth in the Introductory Note of this Current Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">8-K</span> is incorporated by reference into this Item 2.03. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As previously disclosed in the Information Statement, the Company entered into (a)&#160;a five-year senior unsecured revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount equal to $3,000&#160;million (the &#8220;Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility&#8221;) and (b)&#160;a <span style="white-space:nowrap">364-day</span> senior unsecured revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount equal to $1,500&#160;million (the <span style="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;364-Day</span> Revolving Credit Facility&#8221;). Information about the Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility and the <span style="white-space:nowrap">364-Day</span> Revolving Credit Facility can be found in the Information Statement under the sections entitled &#8220;Description of Material Indebtedness&#8212;Credit Facilities&#8212;Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility&#8221; and &#8220;Description of Material Indebtedness&#8212;Credit <span style="white-space:nowrap">Facilities&#8212;364-Day</span> Revolving Credit Facility&#8221;, which sections are incorporated by reference into this Item 2.03. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As previously disclosed in the Information Statement,PHI entered into a loan facility for up to an aggregate principal amount of $3,500&#160;million with Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A. New York Branch on August&#160;26, 2026 (the &#8220;PHI Bilateral Facility&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On October&#160;1, 2026, following the Effective Time, PHI borrowed $1,578&#160;million under the Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility and $1,500&#160;million under the <span style="white-space:nowrap">364-Day</span> Revolving Credit Facility. On October&#160;1, 2026, these proceeds from the Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility and the <span style="white-space:nowrap">364-Day</span> Revolving Credit Facility were used to repay $3,078&#160;million of borrowings under the PHI Bilateral Facility. Following this repayment, on October&#160;1, 2026, the PHI Bilateral Facility ceased to be effective. </p> <p style="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Adoption of Vylor Inc. 2026 Omnibus Incentive Plan and Vylor Inc. 2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In connection with the Separation, the Board adopted, and EIDP, as the Company&#8217;s then-sole stockholder, approved, the Vylor Inc. 2026 Omnibus Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Omnibus Incentive Plan&#8221;) and the Vylor Inc. 2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the &#8220;ESPP&#8221;), in each case, effective as of the Effective Time. A description of the material terms of the Omnibus Incentive Plan and the ESPP can be found in the Information Statement under the section entitled &#8220;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8221;, which description is incorporated by reference into this Item 5.02. The description is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Omnibus Incentive Plan and the ESPP, which are attached as Exhibits 10.1 and 10.2, respectively, to this Current Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">8-K</span> and are incorporated by reference into this Item 5.02. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Adoption of Vylor Inc. Change in Control and Executive Severance Plan </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In connection with the Separation, the Board adopted the Vylor Inc. Change in Control and Executive Severance Plan (the &#8220;Severance Plan&#8221;), effective as of the Effective Time, which provides severance protections to designated employees of the Company, including the Company&#8217;s executive officers. Under the Severance Plan, upon a termination of employment by the Company without cause or by the participant for good reason (for certain tiers, good reason termination applies only during the <span style="white-space:nowrap">two-year</span> period following a change in control (the &#8220;Covered Period&#8221;)), a participant will be eligible to receive (i)&#160;a lump sum cash severance payment equal to an applicable severance multiple (as described below) times the sum of the participant&#8217;s annual base salary and target annual bonus, (ii)&#160;a lump sum cash payment equal to a <span style="white-space:nowrap">pro-rated</span> portion of target annual bonus for the year of termination, (iii)&#160;continued health, dental and vision benefits for the benefits continuation period (as described below) and (iv)&#160;outplacement services. If the qualifying termination occurs during the Covered Period, a participant&#8217;s outstanding equity awards will become fully vested and exercisable with performance conditions deemed achieved at target. Receipt of severance benefits is conditioned on the participant&#8217;s execution of a release of claims and continued compliance with restrictive covenants, including <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-competition</span> and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-solicitation</span> covenants for one year following termination. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#8220;Applicable severance multiple&#8221; means three times for the Chief Executive Officer if the qualifying termination occurs during the Covered Period and two times if the qualifying termination occurs outside of the Covered Period, and ranges from a minimum of one half times to a maximum of two times for other participants depending on tier, years of service, and whether the qualifying termination occurs during the Covered Period. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#8220;Benefits continuation period&#8221; generally means, for the Chief Executive Officer, the period beginning on the date of the qualifying termination and ending three years thereafter if the qualifying termination occurs during the Covered Period, and two years thereafter if the qualifying termination occurs outside of the Covered Period. For other participants, the &#8220;benefits continuation period&#8221; ranges from a minimum of six months to a maximum of two years, depending on tier, years of service, and whether the qualifying termination occurs during the Covered Period. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The description is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Severance Plan, which is attached as Exhibit 10.3 to this Current Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">8-K</span> and is incorporated by reference into this Item 5.02. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Adoption of Vylor Inc. Management Deferred Compensation Plan </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In connection with the Separation, the Board adopted the Vylor Inc. Management Deferred Compensation Plan (the &#8220;Management Deferred Compensation Plan&#8221;), effective as of the Effective Time, which permits a select group of management or highly compensated employees of the Company, including the Company&#8217;s executive officers, to defer receipt of up to 60% of their base salary and up to 60% of their short-term incentive awards. Participants may elect to have their accounts deemed invested in one or more investment options designated by the administrator, including a common stock unit fund. Upon separation from service, change of control, or a specified date elected by the participant, amounts will be distributed in either a lump sum or annual installments for up to ten years, if permitted and as elected by the participant. Benefits under the Management Deferred Compensation Plan are unfunded and are general, unsecured obligations of the Company. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The description is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Management Deferred Compensation Plan, which is attached as Exhibit 10.4 to this Current Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">8-K</span> and is incorporated by reference into this Item 5.02. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Adoption of Vylor Inc. Deferred Compensation and Stock Accumulation Plan for Directors </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In connection with the Separation, the Board adopted the Vylor Inc. Deferred Compensation and Stock Accumulation Plan for Directors (the &#8220;Director Deferred Compensation Plan&#8221;), effective as of the Effective Time, which permits <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</span> directors of the Company to defer, in the form of cash or stock units, all or a specified part of fees </p>
</div></div>



<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
payable to the director for services as a director. Deferred cash bears interest at a rate corresponding to the average <span style="white-space:nowrap">30-year</span> Treasury securities rate applicable for the quarter, compounded quarterly. Fees deferred in the form of stock units are allocated based on the closing price of the Company&#8217;s common stock, with dividend equivalents credited in the form of additional stock units. Upon separation from service or a specified calendar year elected by the director, amounts will be distributed in either a lump sum or annual installments, if permitted and as elected by the director. Benefits under the Director Deferred Compensation Plan are unfunded and are general, unsecured obligations of the Company. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The description is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Director Deferred Compensation Plan, which is attached as Exhibit 10.5 to this Current Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">8-K</span> and is incorporated by reference into this Item 5.02. </p> <p style="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
